companies.name: Armsoftech Private Limited

companies.note: RP-Sanjiv Goenka group BPM (US$1.08 bn FY26 revenue) with a third-party collections line for banks and fintechs and an agentic-AI operating layer; closest listed match for the human-assisted collections seats.

companies.name: Hinduja Global Solutions Ltd
companies.note: Hinduja group voice and non-voice BPM (contact centres, back-office processing) plus a media and communications platform; peer for the seat-based, contact-centre side of the subject's model.

companies.name: eClerx Services Ltd
companies.note: Process management, automation and analytics services to Fortune 2000 clients with financial services as a core vertical; peer for an automation-led, high-margin services model.

companies.name: Nucleus Software Exports Ltd
companies.note: Lending software (FinnOne Neo, including a Gen-AI enabled FinnOne Neo Collections module) for 200+ banks and financial institutions in 50 countries; the most direct product overlap with the subject's collections software.

companies.name: Intellect Design Arena Ltd
companies.note: Chennai banking and insurance software house (core banking, lending, transaction banking, AI platform); peer for a lender-facing software product sold to banks.

companies.note: Hyderabad A2P messaging / CPaaS platform with about 30% of India's CPaaS market; BFSI reminders and borrower communications are the digital channel the subject's voice agent and SMS/WhatsApp nudges sit alongside.

dims.name: Product / technology
dims.why: Armsoftech runs its own AIR Collect stack with a generative-AI voice agent in 13 languages, but it is one product line built on about ₹12 Cr of capitalised development. Intellect and Nucleus have multi-product banking and lending suites sold in dozens of countries; Tanla runs national-scale messaging infrastructure; the BPM peers are services-led with AI layers.

dims.name: Customers and concentration
dims.why: Armsoftech has 35 lender customers with the top three banks at 36% of FY26 revenue. Nucleus serves 200+ banks and financial institutions across 50 countries; Firstsource added 47 new logos in FY26 alone.

dims.name: Entry barriers
dims.why: Collections software and seats can be replaced at contract renewal, and AI voice tools are being launched by many vendors including Nucleus (Gen-AI in FinnOne Neo Collections). Core lending and banking systems (Nucleus, Intellect) and telecom-integrated messaging (Tanla) are much harder to switch out.

dims.name: Distribution / reach
dims.why: Armsoftech sells in India only, to 35 lenders. Firstsource delivers from nine countries; Nucleus operates in 50 countries; Intellect, eClerx and Tanla sell to global or national enterprise client bases.

dims.name: Scale of operations
dims.why: Armsoftech's FY26 revenue of ₹73 Cr is about 8% of Nucleus (₹876 Cr), the smallest peer, and under 1% of Firstsource (₹9,556 Cr, 36,205 employees). Its roughly 2,650 seats compare with tens of thousands at the BPM peers.

dims.name: Management and governance
dims.why: Armsoftech's FY25 audited accounts show ₹19.7 Cr of on-demand related-party loans against ₹5.7 Cr net worth, and the desk has open questions on the financials. Listed peers carry SEBI disclosure and audit-committee oversight; HGS shows ₹2,810 Cr of contingent liabilities and a three-year ROE near 1%.

dims.name: Growth runway
dims.why: Armsoftech grew revenue 20.1% in FY26 and projects ₹101.8 Cr in FY27 (Q1 FY27 ₹19.6 Cr), with India retail and MSME credit expanding the collections pool. Firstsource (22.8% two-year CAGR) and eClerx (18.6%) are growing at a similar pace from far larger bases; HGS and Nucleus grew 5% or less.

dims.name: Collections domain depth
dims.why: Armsoftech is a pure-play collections business covering pre-due to write-off with both software and seats. Firstsource runs third-party collections for US lenders and Nucleus sells a dedicated collections module; for the other peers collections is one use case among many.

dims.name: Regulatory exposure (higher = more insulated)
dims.why: RBI recovery-conduct rules apply directly to lenders' collection agents, so all of Armsoftech's revenue sits in the regulated activity. Firstsource is exposed to US collection rules on part of its book; Tanla to TRAI commercial-communication rules; software vendors are one step removed.

cells: AI collections stack + voice agent + ~2,650 assisted seats
matrix.why: Armsoftech combines software and seats in one collections offer; each peer covers only one side or treats collections as a minor line.
Armsoftech is about one-twelfth the size of the smallest listed peer.
In line with the fastest-growing peers (Firstsource, Intellect, eClerx), ahead of HGS, Nucleus and Tanla.
Highest reported margin in the set, but it is provisional and partly reflects capitalised development spend.
Smaller and more concentrated customer base than any peer.

cells: 9 countries (US, UK, India, Philippines and others)
matrix.why: Single-market exposure; peers diversify currency and regulatory risk.
Voice AI in Indian languages is a specific strength, but every peer now markets an AI layer.

cells: ₹19.7 Cr RPT loans vs ₹5.7 Cr NW (FY25)
matrix.why: Related-party loans of more than three times FY25 net worth are an open diligence item; most peers are near debt-free.
The round's P/E sits at the low end of the set, close to Nucleus and Tanla, against a peer median of 24.3x; the subject's multiple rests on provisional PAT and is unlisted.
No public market for the shares until a listing; six-month post-listing lock-in applies under SEBI ICDR.

barriers.name: Lender integration and onboarding
barriers.note: Plugging into a bank's loan system, allocation rules and audit trails takes months, which slows switching; but with the top three banks at 36% of revenue, losing one contract would be material.

barriers.name: Indian-language voice AI
barriers.note: A generative-AI voice agent in 13 languages trained on collections calls is hard to copy quickly, but large software vendors (Nucleus, Intellect) and CPaaS players are adding similar features.

barriers.name: Regulatory compliance track record
barriers.note: RBI recovery-conduct rules make lenders favour vendors with clean call recording, consent and complaint records; the same rules can tighten and hit the whole sector.

barriers.name: Collections data and scoring models
barriers.note: Repayment-behaviour data from 35 lenders feeds scoring and call prioritisation; peers with 200+ lender clients (Nucleus) or global collections books (Firstsource) have larger data sets.

barriers.name: Seat capacity and trained workforce
barriers.note: About 2,650 human-assisted seats can be replicated by BPM firms with tens of thousands of seats; this is a capacity advantage only against smaller agencies.

barriers.name: Capital and scale
barriers.note: With ₹73 Cr revenue and a ₹30 Cr round, Armsoftech has far less to spend on product and sales than listed peers generating ₹117–1,214 Cr of operating cash flow.

ahead: EBITDA margin of 35.8% (FY26 provisional) against a peer median of 16.6% and a peer high of 25.6% (eClerx).
Revenue growth of 20.1% in FY26 matches the fastest-growing peers (Firstsource 19.7%, Intellect 21.5%, eClerx 22.3%) and is well ahead of Nucleus (5.3%), Tanla (9.7%) and HGS (-2.2%).
A pure-play collections offer from pre-due to write-off, combining software, a 13-language voice agent and about 2,650 seats; no listed peer offers both software and seats focused on collections.
behind: Scale: FY26 revenue of ₹73.0 Cr is about 8% of Nucleus (₹876 Cr), the smallest peer, and under 1% of Firstsource (₹9,556 Cr).
Concentration: 35 lender customers with the top three banks at 36% of FY26 revenue, against 200+ banks and FIs at Nucleus.
Earnings quality: PAT steps up from ₹0.8 Cr (FY25 audited) to ₹10.6 Cr (FY26 provisional), about ₹12 Cr of development is capitalised, and the desk has open questions on the financials.
Governance and balance sheet: ₹19.7 Cr of on-demand related-party loans against ₹5.7 Cr net worth at FY25, while Nucleus, Intellect and Tanla are almost debt-free.
Single-country, single-regulator exposure to RBI recovery-conduct rules; listed peers spread revenue across 9 to 50 countries.
watch: Audited FY26 accounts confirming the ₹10.6 Cr PAT and ₹26.1 Cr EBITDA, and the desk's answers on the open financial questions.
Repayment or settlement of the ₹19.7 Cr related-party loans.
Delivery against the FY27 projection of ₹101.8 Cr revenue and ₹14.7 Cr PAT (Q1 FY27: ₹19.6 Cr revenue).
Any change in RBI recovery-conduct rules, and customer additions that bring the top-three share below 36%.
valuation: At the round, P/E FY26 is 14.2x and market cap / EBITDA 5.7x, against peer medians of 24.3x and 13.9x; price / sales of 2.05x is in line with the peer median of about 2.0x.
